findings.explanation: The new session-binding helper `session_key_for_request` (base.py:62-82) derives the binding key from `request.auth` when present, but `request.auth` is set by the API authentication layer for ANY authenticated API caller (OAuth access token, OAuth application, TeamAPIToken, Device). The key is then only the token/application/device primary key (e.g. `app:<pk>`, `token:<pk>`, `device:<pk>`), with no organizer/event scoping. `allowed_for_session` (base.py:84-88) returns True whenever the caller's auth object matches the stored key. Because the key is not scoped to the organizer/event that owns the CachedFile, a caller authenticated with a token that has access to a DIFFERENT organizer/event can pass the session check and download a CachedFile belonging to another organizer/event (IDOR / broken object-level authorization). The base code already had this pattern (e.g. api/views/shredders.py:71 `session_key=f'api-shredder-{type}-{pk}'`), but this PR centralizes and generalizes it into a reusable helper that is now applied to the generic CachedFile download path (base/views/cachedfiles.py:39 `if not o.allowed_for_session(self.request)`), newly exposing the unscoped comparison to the web download view. The policy (permissions.rst) requires fine-grained, organizer/event-scoped permission checks; a bare token pk is not such a check.

evidence.content: pretix uses a fine-grained permission system to control who is allowed to control what parts of the system. ... A team can be assigned a set of permissions and connected to some or all of the events of the organizer.

findings.suggested_fix: Scope the session binding key to the organizer/event that owns the CachedFile (e.g. include the organizer/event pk in the key, or verify the caller has permission on the file's organizer/event before allowing the download), rather than comparing only the raw token/application/device pk. Ensure `allowed_for_session` also enforces that the requester is authorized for the specific object's organizer/event.

findings.explanation: The changed line fetches a CachedFile by a user-controlled identifier (request.POST.get("background")) and only filters by web_download=True. The CachedFile model has no owner/event/organizer field (base.py lines 49-60), so web_download=True is not an ownership check — it is a global flag shared by all web-downloadable files. The view's own download path (base/views/cachedfiles.py lines 38-40) additionally enforces allowed_for_session(request), but this lookup does not, so a user with 'can_change_settings' on one event can reference a CachedFile id belonging to another event/organizer and use it as the ticket background (override_background=cf.file) or persist it via save_background(cf). This is an IDOR: the object is fetched by a user-controlled id without verifying the requester owns it.

evidence.content:
class CachedFile(models.Model):
    id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
    expires = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    date = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    filename = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    type = models.CharField(max_length=255)
    file = models.FileField(null=True, blank=True, upload_to=_cachedfile_name, max_length=255)
    web_download = models.BooleanField(default=True)  # allow web download, True for backwards compatibility in plugins
    session_key = models.TextField(null=True, blank=True)  # only allow download in this session

class MyEventView(EventPermissionRequiredMixin, View):
    permission = 'can_change_event_settings'
    # Only users with the permission ``can_change_event_settings`` on
    # this event can access this

findings.suggested_fix: Scope the lookup to the current event/organizer (e.g. filter by the event's background setting or a session_key bound to the request) and/or enforce o.allowed_for_session(request) before using cf, so a user cannot reference a CachedFile belonging to another event/organizer.
